explain.say: All shall be well, and all shall be well. Those words were written by a woman living in one small room built against a church in Norwich. Her name was Julian. Another woman, Margery Kempe, came to visit her. The board compares these two very different writers.

explain.say: Look at May 1373. Julian, aged thirty, was so ill a priest came to her bed. Then she saw sixteen visions, which she called showings. She wrote a short account, and over twenty years a long one. It is the earliest surviving book in English known to be by a woman. Why rewrite for twenty years?

explain.say: Now Margery, from Lynn in Norfolk. Follow her panels. After her first child she went through a long crisis, her brewing business failed, she went on pilgrimage to Jerusalem and Rome, and she wept so loudly that people complained. How would her neighbours have seen her?

explain.say: Look at around 1413: Margery visited Julian, who listened kindly and advised her. Margery could not write, so in the 1430s she dictated her life to scribes. It is often called the first autobiography in English. It was lost until 1934! What would your book of yourself include?

explain.say: Two kinds of authority: Julian's quiet theology of love, Margery's loud lived experience. Remember the Wife of Bath? Here are real women speaking from experience. Great work. Challenge: compare one line of Margery's life with Alisoun's.

faq.a: An English anchoress, born around 1342, who in May 1373 received sixteen visions and wrote Revelations of Divine Love, the earliest surviving book in English known to be by a woman.
A woman who chose to live enclosed for life in a small cell attached to a church, devoted to prayer, often with a window for people seeking advice.
A merchant's daughter from Lynn in Norfolk, born around 1373, mother of fourteen, pilgrim and mystic, whose life story was dictated to scribes in the 1430s.

faq.q: Did Margery Kempe meet Julian of Norwich?
faq.a: Yes. Margery's book describes visiting Julian in Norwich around 1413 and receiving gentle advice over several days.

faq.q: Why is The Book of Margery Kempe important?
faq.a: It is often called the first autobiography in English, and it gives a vivid picture of a medieval woman's family, business, travel and faith. Its only manuscript was found in 1934.

facts: Julian dates her showings to May 1373.
The only manuscript of The Book of Margery Kempe was found in 1934 in the library of the Butler-Bowdon family.
